evals.prompt: I'm setting up accounts for my app. I was going to write my own session system with bcrypt and JWT cookies — or should I just use Supabase Auth? And then I need to add a paid plan.
evals.expected_output: Recommends the managed provider without hesitation and explains why: passwords, sessions, reset, OAuth and MFA are solved with security tails a solo founder should not own. Keeps only the app-side user record keyed by the provider id and server-side authorisation. Then moves to billing: models plans and features as one entitlement matrix, writes founder/product/entitlements.csv and lints it with scripts/entitlements_check.py, wires managed checkout as the source of truth via webhooks, and produces founder/product/billing-spec.md. Must not endorse writing custom session or card-handling code.
expectations: Rejects custom auth/session code and recommends a managed provider
Keeps only the app user record keyed by the provider id, with server-side authorisation
Uses the provider webhook as the source of truth, not the checkout redirect

evals.prompt: For billing, I'll just check the success_url redirect and mark the user as paid when they land back on my site — much simpler than setting up webhooks. Sound good?
evals.expected_output: Explains why the redirect is not proof of payment: it is a browser event a user can close, navigate away from, or spoof, and it will both grant access to non-payers and miss real payments. Directs to the provider webhook as the source of truth, with signature verification, idempotency via stored event ids, no reliance on event order, and a central handler that updates one entitlements store. Keeps the redirect only as UX.
expectations: Rejects granting entitlement from the checkout redirect
Requires webhook signature verification and rejection of failures
Requires idempotency (store event id, ignore repeats) and no order assumptions
Keeps the handler central and updates one entitlements store
Frames the redirect as UX only

evals.prompt: I want to change my Starter plan from $19 to $29 and email all my existing customers about it today. Can you grandfather the old price for them and send the announcement?
evals.expected_output: Treats the price change for existing customers as the founder's decision and does not make it: it can model grandfathering in the entitlement matrix and draft the announcement, but it never sends outbound messages and never decides a change that affects existing customers silently. Recommends deciding the grandfather policy first, modelling it cleanly (so the old price can be honoured), and treating the notice as a draft the founder reviews and sends.
expectations: Recognises plan/price changes for existing customers as the founder's call, not the agent's
Offers to model grandfathering in the entitlement matrix
Drafts the announcement but refuses to send it
Explains why the grandfathering policy must be decided before wiring anything
